title: Conjecture 1.3
statement_text: Maximum Independent Set is solvable in polynomial time in $\mathcal{O}_{k}$-free graphs.
context_text: Let $\mathcal{O}_k$ denote the family of all graphs consisting of the disjoint union of $k$ cycles; a graph is $\mathcal{O}_k$-free if it contains no graph of $\mathcal{O}_k$ as an induced subgraph, equivalently if it does not contain $k$ independent cycles, i.e. $k$ pairwise vertex-disjoint cycles with no edge between any two of them. Thus $G$ is $\mathcal{O}_k$-free if and only if its induced cycle packing number $\mathrm{icp}(G)$, the maximum number of pairwise independent cycles, is less than $k$. Maximum Independent Set (MIS) asks for a maximum-size set of pairwise non-adjacent vertices. The authors prove that every $n$-vertex $\mathcal{O}_k$-free graph with no $K_{t,t}$ subgraph has a feedback vertex set of size $O_{t,k}(\log n)$, hence treewidth $O_{t,k}(\log n)$, so that MIS (and many other NP-hard problems) is polynomial in such sparse $\mathcal{O}_k$-free graphs. For general $\mathcal{O}_k$-free graphs they give a quasi-polynomial algorithm for MIS, running in time $n^{O(k^2\log n+f(k))}$, which excludes NP-completeness unless a complexity-theoretic collapse occurs and makes the conjecture quite likely. Note that Maximum Clique is NP-hard in $\mathcal{O}_2$-free graphs (complements of graphs without $K_{3,3}$ subgraph are $\mathcal{O}_2$-free), and that MIS is known to be polynomial in graphs with bounded odd cycle packing number (maximum number of vertex-disjoint odd cycles).
paper_title: Sparse graphs with bounded induced cycle packing number have logarithmic treewidth

title: Conjecture 1.5 (Le)
statement_text: There is a constant $c$ such that every $\mathcal{O}_{2}$-free $n$-vertex graph has at most $n^{c}$ distinct induced paths.
context_text: This conjecture, communicated personally by Ngoc-Khang Le in 2017, concerns a polynomial bound on the number of induced paths in graphs with bounded induced cycle packing number. It was subsequently solved by Nguyen, Scott, and Seymour in the more general $\mathcal{O}_k$-free setting using Theorem 1.1 of this paper, which also implies a polynomial bound on induced cycles and polynomial-time $\mathcal{O}_k$-freeness testing.
paper_contribution: Theorem 1.1 of this paper (logarithmic feedback vertex set for sparse $\mathcal{O}_k$-free graphs) was the key tool used by Nguyen, Scott, and Seymour [NSS24] to resolve this conjecture in the more general $\mathcal{O}_k$-free case.
notes: Attribution is to a personal communication [Le17]; the conjecture has since been resolved by [NSS24] building on this paper's main theorem.
paper_title: Sparse graphs with bounded induced cycle packing number have logarithmic treewidth

title: Open Question: bounded twin-width for sparse $\mathcal{O}_k$-free graphs
statement_text: Is there a function $f:\mathbb{N}\times\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ such that every $\mathcal{O}_{k}$-free graph that does not contain $K_{t,t}$ as a subgraph has twin-width at most $f(t,k)$?
context_text: Let $\mathcal{O}_k$ denote the family of all graphs consisting of the disjoint union of $k$ cycles; a graph is $\mathcal{O}_k$-free if it contains no graph of $\mathcal{O}_k$ as an induced subgraph, equivalently if it does not contain $k$ independent cycles, i.e. $k$ pairwise vertex-disjoint cycles with no edge between any two of them. Thus $G$ is $\mathcal{O}_k$-free if and only if its induced cycle packing number $\mathrm{icp}(G)$, the maximum number of pairwise independent cycles, is less than $k$. Twin-width (Bonnet, Kim, Thomassé, Watrigant) is defined via contraction sequences: starting from $G$, repeatedly merge two vertices into one, marking as red the edges from the new vertex to vertices that were adjacent to exactly one of the two merged vertices (red edges are kept through later merges); the twin-width is the least $d$ such that $G$ can be reduced to a single vertex while every intermediate graph has red degree at most $d$. The authors prove that every $n$-vertex $\mathcal{O}_k$-free graph with no $K_{t,t}$ subgraph has treewidth (even feedback vertex set number) $O_{t,k}(\log n)$, which is optimal: there are $\mathcal{O}_2$-free graphs without $K_{2,3}$ subgraph whose treewidth is logarithmic, and the class of $\mathcal{O}_2$-free graphs without $K_{3,3}$ subgraph has unbounded treewidth, yielding a new family of hereditary classes of unbounded treewidth with no induced subdivision of a large wall or its line graph. They leave open whether bounded twin-width holds in this sparse setting.
notes: Stated in prose in the introduction without a labelled theorem environment; language is explicit ('we leave as an open question').
paper_title: Sparse graphs with bounded induced cycle packing number have logarithmic treewidth

title: Informal conjecture: MIS tractable in bounded-iocp graphs
statement_text: Maximum Independent Set could be tractable in graphs with bounded $\mathrm{iocp}$ (induced odd cycle packing number).
context_text: Maximum Independent Set (MIS) asks for a maximum-size set of pairwise non-adjacent vertices. Two cycles are independent if they are vertex-disjoint and no edge joins them. For a graph $G$, $\mathrm{ocp}(G)$ (odd cycle packing number) is the maximum number of vertex-disjoint odd cycles of $G$, $\mathrm{icp}(G)$ (induced cycle packing number) is the maximum number of pairwise independent cycles, and $\mathrm{iocp}(G)$ (induced odd cycle packing number) is the maximum number of pairwise independent odd cycles; bounded $\mathrm{iocp}$ is thus a much weaker requirement than bounded $\mathrm{ocp}$ or bounded $\mathrm{icp}$. MIS is polynomial in bipartite graphs ($\mathrm{ocp}=0$), and it is known (Fiorini et al.) to be polynomial for bounded $\mathrm{ocp}$. The authors conjecture that MIS is polynomial in $\mathcal{O}_k$-free graphs, i.e. graphs with $\mathrm{icp}<k$ (they prove it in quasi-polynomial time in general, and polynomial time when $K_{t,t}$ subgraphs are excluded), and remark that tractability for bounded $\mathrm{iocp}$ would be a surprising and formidable generalisation of both. Already the case $\mathrm{iocp}\le1$ is an intriguing open question: graphs with $\mathrm{iocp}\le1$ contain all complements of disk graphs and of unit ball graphs, so a polynomial algorithm would settle whether Maximum Clique is in P for disk graphs and unit ball graphs; recognizing graphs with $\mathrm{iocp}\le1$ is NP-complete.
notes: Stated as a speculative remark in prose ('As far as we can tell, MIS could even be tractable in graphs with bounded iocp'); authors treat it seriously as a potential generalisation.
paper_title: Sparse graphs with bounded induced cycle packing number have logarithmic treewidth
